name: Breakout of yesterday's range
idea: When the price breaks above yesterday's high (or below its low), jump in. The move should keep going.
headline: PDR break 2R

name: Overnight range breakout (the "Asian range")
idea: Mark the high and low of the quiet overnight session. Trade the break when Europe or New York opens.
headline: ON range break 2R

name: Fading the overnight range (a reversal)
idea: The opposite bet: when the price pokes out of the overnight range, expect it to fall back in.
headline: ON range fade

name: Gap fill
idea: When the market opens far from yesterday's close, bet that it drifts back to close the gap.
headline: Gap fill > 0.5 range

name: Gap and go
idea: The opposite of gap fill: a big opening gap means strong buyers, so follow it.
headline: Gap continue > 0.25

name: Narrow-range breakout (NR7)
idea: After the quietest day of the last seven, a big move often follows. Trade the break of that quiet day's range.
headline: NR7 breakout 2.5R
comment: The closest of the chart patterns: it made money in all four markets. But with only 892 trades, a t of 1.10 is well within what luck produces.

name: VWAP reversion
idea: VWAP is the day's average price, weighted by volume. When the price stretches far from it, bet on the snap back.
headline: VWAP revert 2.0 sd

name: VWAP trend
idea: When the price crosses above the day's average price, the buyers are in control. Go with them.
headline: VWAP trend cross

name: Late-day momentum (and its reverse)
idea: If the day has been strong, the last hour continues it, because funds finish their buying. The fade version bets the opposite.
headline: Late-day momentum

name: ICT: liquidity sweep and fair value gap
idea: Wait for the price to dip below a recent low ("sweeping the liquidity"), then shoot up and leave a gap. Buy when it comes back into the gap.
headline: ict
comment: Coded exactly as taught (the 2022 model), on 8 markets. Tested separately and audited, unlike the rest of this gallery.
